simple.meaning: נִיר (nîyr) is a Hebrew action word meaning “to till the soil.” BibleIQ anchors the English reading to this source verb before comparing its uses.
simple.biblicalBackground: This action appears 2 times in Jeremiah, Hosea, beginning at Jeremiah 4:3. The surrounding contexts include righteousness.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to נִיר (H5214) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Actions in Scripture show what people do, what God does, and how covenant faithfulness or rebellion is described. BibleIQ compares the action across its occurrences.
simple.summary: נִיר (nîyr) / H5214 is traced through Jeremiah 4:3, Hosea 10:12 with source-language evidence and verse context.

definitions.full: H5214. nir I. [ נִיר ] verb break up, freshly till ; — Qal Imperative masculine plural נִ֫ירוּ , with accusative of congnate meaning with verb נִיר Hosea 10:12 ; Jer 4:3 .
definitions.rootNote: a root probably identical with that of 5216 , through the idea of the gleam of a fresh furrow;

occurrences.englishText: For Yahweh says to the men of Judah and to Jerusalem, “Break up your fallow ground, and don’t sow among thorns.
